title: Made of Air
text:
Made out of the air
+
+between pine trees and the rocks
+
+the poem springs forth.
editorial_note: The English keeps the miniature’s 5–7–5 syllabic shape while preserving the poem’s sudden organic emergence from air and stone.

title: Interwoven
text:
Interwoven,
+
+vowels and consonants:
+
+house of the world.
editorial_note: The grammatical suspension is retained: letters are at once woven material and the dwelling they construct for the world.

title: What I Say
text:
What I am saying
+
+is scarcely three lines:
+
+a hut of syllables.
editorial_note: The self-describing three-line poem remains deliberately modest: language is not a monument but a small inhabitable shelter.

title: Logs and Straw
text:
Logs and straw;
+
+through the cracks come in
+
+Buddhas and insects.
editorial_note: The same humble openings admit enlightenment and ordinary life; the plural Buddhas is kept without interpretive expansion.

title: Upon the Sand
text:
Upon the sand,
+
+the writing of birds:
+
+memories of wind.
editorial_note: Tracks become writing and their erasure becomes the wind’s memory; the compact chain of transformations is left unqualified.

title: The Exclamation
text:
Still
+
+not upon the branch
+
+in the air
+
+Not in the air
+
+in the instant
+
+the hummingbird
editorial_note: Quieto remains the paradoxical stillness of a hovering bird; punctuation is not added, allowing the hummingbird itself to arrive as the final exclamation.

title: Objects
text:
They live beside us,
+
+we ignore them, they ignore us.
+
+Sometimes they speak with us.
editorial_note: The reciprocal ignorar is mirrored exactly; the final conversation remains an occasional breach in the quiet autonomy of things.

title: The Birds Sing, They Sing…
text:
The birds sing, they sing
+
+without knowing what they sing:
+
+all their understanding is their throat.
editorial_note: Entendimiento remains understanding rather than thought: the poem locates avian knowledge entirely in the bodily act of song.
